sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 26 = check 25; Internal Quality Checks row 26 = check 25, no further annotation columns filled)

.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/task/tests/{gates,scored}/*/judge.toml ([judge] and mcp_servers blocks; gate criteria in full; scored criteria by keyword scan and the opening criteria only, not all 43 functional criteria line by line)
evidence: Skill check 25 asks that every prompt opens http://localhost:3000 and directs the judge to the Playwright MCP tool. All five frozen prompts do so on line 1: constraints/prompt.md:1 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP. Use only rendered browser behavior and the live DOM.'; render/prompt.md:1 '... using Playwright MCP. Use only rendered browser behavior.'; functional/prompt.md:1, polish/prompt.md:1 and visual/prompt.md:1 open with the same 'Evaluate the live Colderwater playground at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP.' Each of the five judge.toml files wires a 'playwright' MCP server (playwright-mcp, headless chromium), so the tool the prompts name exists. Not from source: functional/prompt.md:22 'do not read implementation files to infer success'; polish/prompt.md:19 'do not read implementation files'; visual/prompt.md:20 'Do not read implementation files and do not infer behavior from styling'; constraints/prompt.md:5 'decide it from the listed DOM facts only, not from file names, bundled library names or how the code looks'; render is limited to 'only rendered browser behavior'. Not from memory: functional/prompt.md:11 and polish/prompt.md:11 'A criterion passes only on evidence you gathered yourself in this session for that criterion. If you did not perform a step, that step did not pass.'; visual/prompt.md:15 'never invent an observation'; constraints/prompt.md:5 'if a step could not be performed say so plainly and fail that criterion rather than assuming it passed'. Not from first paint: the three scored prompts carry a global browser gate requiring 'that text typed into the code editor appears in it' (line 5 of each); the render criterion requires clicking in, typing a word with real keys and reloading; the first constraints criterion requires typing a word before inspecting the DOM; visual/prompt.md:13-14 requires a resize to about 1440 by 900, a ten-line draft, one Run, a click with a two-second caret watch, a double-click selection and screenshots before scoring. The opening sentences match the frozen template's wording pattern. Weak-app probe: a static screenshot-like shell cannot pass any dimension because every dimension requires typed text to appear; conforming-alternative probe: a canvas-drawn editor is still gradeable because app_context.md:29 directs reading from screenshots. Evidence index: all 16 scripted-golden artifacts match their raw-byte SHA256 and all 6 hosted-run JSON files match their LF-normalised SHA256. Notes (not defects): (1) the two gate prompts forbid source-based judging by scope ('Use only rendered browser behavior') rather than with an explicit 'do not read implementation files' sentence as the three scored prompts have; the scope sentence is equivalent in effect and mirrors the template. (2) Whether the configured judge actually obeys these directions on these bytes is unmeasured: the scripted golden run is not a judge run, and the hosted judge run was on an earlier candidate whose prompts were later reworded; I did not inspect judge trajectories. This row's check is a property of the prompt text, so that gap does not change the verdict, but no judge-behaviour claim is made. (3) I did not read all 43 functional criterion descriptions line by line; a keyword scan for source/shell/health wording found only browser-side uses (functional/judge.toml:173 'not CSS selectors or source files', :326 loading the health address in a normal browser tab).
